Name: Auto Factory
Description:
[h2]Auto Factory[/h2]

Ever built an impressive industrial deck, stocked every ingredient, and still found yourself babysitting production queues one recipe at a time? Meet a suspiciously enthusiastic cloud of industrial Nanobots.

Auto Factory adds the Tier 4 [b]Nano Foundry[/b], Tier 5 [b]Nano Fabricator[/b], and Tier 5 [b]Nano Cloning Pod[/b]. They reproduce eligible high-throughput recipes, respond to material shortages, and maintain prioritized global inventory goals while preserving normal Stardeus crafting and Being lifecycles.

[h2]Facilities[/h2]

[h3]Nano Foundry[/h3]
- Recreates the best Furnace Ore and Burnable recipes in an isolated recipe family
- Uses the original ingredients plus Nanobot fuel

[h3]Nano Fabricator[/h3]
- Recreates eligible advanced recipes from other crafting facilities
- Supports Components, equipment, upgrades, ammunition, Weapons, non-biological robotic body parts, and Fabricator-produced Beings
- Discovers eligible robotic products from Core definitions instead of fixed product lists
- Produces eligible missing intermediaries when the requested product cannot yet be crafted
- Excludes Converter routes, Cloning Pod products, and unrelated Ore, Plants, Food Ingredients, and Food production

[h3]Nano Cloning Pod[/h3]
- Recreates the best Human, Animal, and Organics Cloning Pod recipes in an isolated recipe family
- Produces materials, eggs, body parts, biological Beings, and other products through Core's normal crafting output path
- Can request missing intermediaries from a compatible Nano Fabricator or Nano Foundry
- Requires Nanobots and the source recipe's normal ingredients

[h2]Native Building Replacement[/h2]

Overlay a Nano Foundry ghost on a constructed Furnace, a Nano Fabricator on a Fabricator, or a Nano Cloning Pod on a Cloning Pod to queue a native replacement. The replacement keeps the footprint, rotation rules, ports, and object layer. Core remains responsible for hauling, construction, cancellation, supported configuration copying, removal of the old building, and electrical reconnection.

[h2]Production Automation[/h2]

[h3]Material Demand and Production Goals[/h3]
- Responds to native Room- and Global-scope Lacking materials demand before Production Goals
- Provides a global inventory target and saved priority from 0 to 100 for every eligible material, object, and Being product
- Handles higher-priority unmet goals first and carries that priority through eligible intermediary work
- Counts stored and equipped objects where appropriate, biological Beings by exact active definition, and robotic inventory as available coreless chassis plus active player-faction robots
- Coordinates owned inventory, pending output, and assigned work so multiple facilities do not blindly duplicate a goal
- Uses bounded planning and retries deferred routes on later safe ticks
- Keeps one Produce One order per managed facility and clears completed automated orders before scheduling another
- Treats a player-selected recipe as a one-cycle manual override, then returns to automation

[h3]Reusable Production Goals Tables[/h3]
- Save the current Goal and Priority values as a named table for reuse across playthroughs
- Load a table to replace the current grid or update the loaded table with the separate Save action
- Maintain multiple tables and delete unwanted entries without clearing the current grid
- Clear all production goals resets the grid and unloads the selected table without changing its saved copy

[h3]Throughput-Ranked Recipes[/h3]
- Ranks routes by batch output per adjusted Auto Factory production hour
- Exposes the highest-throughput route or equal-best ties for each product and facility
- Selects a craftable route from tied options and preserves all tied routes for dependency searches
- Retains hidden load-only aliases for retired recipe IDs so older in-flight orders can load safely

[h3]Global and Room Scope[/h3]
- Gives every managed facility an independent Global or Room automation scope
- Adds a Scope action for setting multiple selected Nano facilities together
- Global facilities respond to ship-wide shortages and inventory
- Room facilities handle shortages from their enclosed room, then help with unmet global Production Goals while idle
- Pauses Room automation when a facility is not enclosed instead of silently changing its scope
- Keeps ingredients ship-wide so normal hauling can supply Room-scoped facilities from eligible storage

[h2]Interface and Persistence[/h2]

- Adds a cooperative top-bar widget and resizable Auto Factory panel through Auto Utilities Mod Framework
- Provides Overview and Production Goals tabs, facility counts, active-order status, Nanobot reserves, and shared task priority
- Organizes products into searchable, independently collapsible categories
- Presents compact Item, Owned, Goal, and Priority columns with numeric bounds and immediate clear-to-zero behavior
- Saves automation enablement, priorities, Production Goals, facility scope, pending deliveries, and in-flight order ownership
- Preserves scope, labels, and order classification through relocation and save/load
- Records queueing, completion, cancellation, manual override, shortage, and cross-facility activity in each facility's Log tab

[h2]Important Behavior[/h2]

All three facilities consume the original recipe ingredients at 110% of source energy cost and require 0.0625 Nanobots per active production hour. Production Goals may finish slightly above their target when a recipe produces multiple items. Newly available routes normally react on the next safe planning tick; in large saves, bounded deferred checks may rotate over several ticks instead of blocking one simulation frame.

Auto Factory does not weaken Core recipe validation, fuel handling, task priorities, hauling, storage compatibility, Being creation, or explosion behavior. Each facility retains Nanobot refill storage as its sole active explosiveness provider.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]

Requires [b]Auto Utilities Mod Framework 1.4.0[/b] for the top-bar widget, managed panel, compatibility handshake, theme-aware controls, scrolling, collapsible sections, and guarded shortcut assignment.

Nano Smelting requires Smelting and Nanobots. Nano Fabrication requires Advanced Assembly and Nanobots. Nano Cloning requires Genetic Engineering and Nanobots.

[h2]In Short[/h2]

You choose the scope, stockpile goals, and which products matter most. Stardeus supplies the ingredients and workers. Core creates the products, Beings, and replacement jobs. The Nanobots keep the best eligible production route moving.

[b]One order at a time. No recipe alchemy. Much less queue babysitting.[/b]
